approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves task-local molecular graphs from scored survivors, drawing parents across score quantiles and using connected-fragment crossover and bounded mutation walks. It admits canonical, valid, fresh offspring into a complete surplus pool, fits a Gaussian process to every earlier accepted score using folded chirality-aware Morgan occurrence counts, and allocates the next batch by correlated sampled function values. It keeps score-greedy survivors and a full chronological learning archive. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled.
approach.novelty: Replace the dot-product count Tanimoto covariance with min/max count Tanimoto, retaining the same occurrence rows. This changes how repeated environments determine overlap without removing counts, unfolding their coordinates, adding the atom-pair channel, or changing allocation. The two laws agree on binary rows, so repeated-count exposure and changed actual selections must be measured. The mathematical validity of min/max overlap permits this experiment; it does not predict a gain.

observed_bottleneck: The current exchange-free Parent conditions on all earlier accepted scores using squared-count dot-product Tanimoto and samples correlated function values over a full fresh graph pool. Its complete matched baseline has macro mean 0.5956696497334577 and population SD 0.02659287062806747; the baseline audit records 629 strict best-parent beats and 258 incumbent gains among 4350 accepted offspring. This identifies limited productive delivery, not proof that squared-count geometry is the cause. Removing counts (n-e00db808bbb4) loses 0.051295849138213355, so retain multiplicity. Count unfolding (n-b14daceabbeb) loses 0.04816296717262832; equal atom-pair mixing (n-e75f0f495f9b) loses 0.033408159038087325 despite some improved selected-stream predictions. Generation-order allocation (n-01b48dd09404) loses 0.12438789088524467 while increasing local parent beats: raw local success alone does not establish better endpoint discovery. These specific controls motivate an isolated overlap-law test, without transferring count-presence contribution to a replacement covariance.
hypothesis: Replace dot-product count Tanimoto covariance by exact min/max count Tanimoto K(x,y)=sum_i min(x_i,y_i)/sum_i max(x_i,y_i) on unchanged folded Morgan occurrence rows, with empty/empty=1 and empty/nonempty=0.

finding_summary.headline: Selections changed throughout, but ranking weakened and all three seed macros fell
finding_summary.insights: This was an exposed covariance intervention: repeated counts were present, all three Gram systems moved, the inherited allocator delivered different candidates, and the numerical and identity audits found no execution failure. Its activation is confirmed; its predicted ranking and endpoint benefit is contradicted under this Parent and profile. Lower MSE against the actual Parent stream did not signify better search: the child sampled lower absolute offspring/source scores, and the original GP fit to the exact same child state predicted its chosen scores better overall. Farther-from-archive accepted pairs and some individual task/seed cells provide positive ranking or local-win counterexamples, but they do not rescue the failed complete gain test or reveal rewards of unselected candidates. Rich aromatic, carbonyl and amine organization remained alongside reactive nitrogen attachments, difficult bridges and unspecified stereochemistry; the molecular evidence does not isolate a covariance-mediated chemical cause. The result closes this exact min/max law without transferring the failure to all count kernels or to those generator gaps. Mean-versus-covariance mediation, independent plausible scaffold supply and broader contribution remain open; terminal records and overlapping ancestry limit continuation claims.
finding_summary.results: The changed posterior reached every batch: all 435 selection orders changed against the passive original GP, and 433 selected sets changed. All 4,350 emitted offspring were accepted with their logged identities. On those same scored offspring, pair-order accuracy was 70.68% versus 71.51% for the passive original model, mean batch Spearman was 0.522 versus 0.536, and prediction MSE was 0.009562 versus 0.009146. Productive search also weakened overall: 623 offspring beat their best generating parent versus 629 for the actual Parent; sequential incumbent gains fell from 258 to 232, and beats of the whole-batch pre-feedback incumbent fell from 346 to 311. Mean offspring and source scores fell, while generic-core novelty on parent-beating events rose slightly from 190 to 195. Final macro mean fell from 0.595670 to 0.547424, a matched change of -0.048245 rather than the required +0.002. Seed macro differences were -0.083646, -0.018090 and -0.043000. Three of fifteen task/seed endpoints improved; twelve declined. Seed dispersion narrowed from 0.026593 to 0.007300 around the lower mean.

molecular.headline: Rich aromatic and fused-ring chemistry persists, with reactive nitrogen substitutions, difficult bridges and undefined stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: Child n-dd2b25d32925 was assessed against the accepted published code Parent n-62daf219c70a. All supplied Child and Parent Search trajectories were read in full; every task and seed is covered and no supplied trajectory path is missing. context.comparison reports both child_complete=true and paired_complete=true for seeds 0, 1 and 2, with no profile mismatch. This is a complete matched comparison on the exchange-disabled L01 graph/count-GP Parent at 300 observations per task, including ten initial, batch ten and the frozen Research in Depth profile. The supplied macro means are 0.547424387911938 for Child and 0.5956696497334577 for Parent; signed seed macro differences are -0.08364553981417, -0.01809049406612706 and -0.04299975158426195. These numbers describe the supplied comparison, not a molecular activation or selection decision. The output contains indole-like aryl amides, linked nitrogen-rich aromatic carbonyl systems, bridged/cyclic basic amines with aromatic appendages, fused nitrogen-dicarbonyl frameworks, and fluorinated nitrogen-carbonyl/enamine chains. Each task digest covers 900 observations and 870 optimizer proposals. Ring-closure-text incidence is 0.9598 to 0.9931 and aromatic-text incidence 0.923 to 0.9828. These are molecule-level incidences of SMILES features, not perceived ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions. Potentially useful ring and amine chemistry is present, but local N-halogen/N-S environments, small-ring unsaturation, crowded bridges and very large recombined structures make overall plausibility questionable. Diversity is moderate across tasks and seeds; leaders within seeds often retain close scaffold families. Formal charge is nearly absent, but neutral aliphatic amines are visibly present; neutral strings do not establish nonbasic molecules. Stereocentre-text incidence is 0.0 for every task despite potentially stereogenic saturated and bridged centres. Missing stereochemical identity is observable; a reward penalty, accessible conformation, stability, route or biological activity is not established. The digest final_molecules are the last seed-2 proposals, not all seed endpoints. Published Parent trajectories are authoritative for comparisons but are absent from context.citation_trajectory_paths, so Parent-only SMILES are deliberately excluded from cited_smiles. Historical gap ancestry was read through context.evidence_index from n-c55c3d520a2c and n-62daf219c70a; the same-code baseline carries those original gaps and conditions. Current re-observation does not attribute them to the covariance replacement or any retained component. The read-only support audit is .slots/round-0026-slot-0/molecular-evidence-audit.json. Actual logged parent draws and accepted direct descendant identities distinguish realized use from mere graph novelty, but overlapping generating parents do not identify donated atoms or causal chemical inheritance. Nonuse does not distinguish lack of survivor support from supported-but-undrawn records; terminal proposals have no later breeding opportunity. No unscored pool member has a known reward, and this report does not claim kernel mediation, calibration or a component contribution. The actual accepted-emission join records 623 strict best-parent beats and 232 incumbent gains for Child, versus 629 and 258 for Parent, among 4350 offspring per panel. Actual later parent draws occur for 2349 Child records and 2401 Parent records; 1851 and 1799 nonterminal records respectively are never drawn later. Each panel has 150 terminal records, with 92 Child and 97 Parent immediate survivor admissions; these are censored opportunities, not measured useful continuations. Child has 261 parent-beating records with a later direct accepted parent-beating child and 112 incumbent-gain records with a later direct incumbent-gain child; Parent has 282 and 122. These overlapping identity-based categories demonstrate some productive continuation without establishing independent discoveries or chemical causation. All current seed leaders beat their logged best generating parent and the pre-feedback incumbent, but later direct accepted children of those final leaders do not exceed the leader. Five Child leaders arise in the last observed batch and have no future-use opportunity. These event counts are derived from trajectory-matched real observed scores and logged source identities in the support audit; they are not molecular quality scores.

per_task.generated_character: Mostly compact to medium fused aromatic frameworks connected through an amide to phenyl or pyridyl rings. Seed 2's leader is a methoxy/amino/methyl fused nitrogen system bearing an N-S-substituted aryl amide; seed 1 retains a substituted indole and pyridyl amide but attaches chlorine directly to the amide nitrogen. Seed 0 develops a bridged indole-like core with a hydroxyl centre and a cyclic hydrazine-containing amide region. Thus ring chemistry is abundant, including nonaromatic bridges, rather than just isolated aromatic fragments. Mean proposal SMILES length is 44.6, with halogen-text incidence 0.7655. Conventional aryl amides coexist with N-S, N-N and N-Cl chemistry and topology that is not routinely supported by a synthetic route. Parent leaders instead include N-halogen indole derivatives, a diketone and a cumulene family; neither panel demonstrates consistently conventional local chemistry.
liabilities: Amide N-Cl and N-S bonds are distinct from ordinary aromatic carbon-bound halogens and require local reactivity assessment.
Hydrazine-containing and bridged relatives raise stability and geometry questions that graph validity cannot answer.
Late proposals still include single atoms, small reactive fragments and an unusual charged diazene-like amide representation.
missing_features: Stable, conventional nitrogen substitution retaining the favorable aromatic/amide arrangement is not demonstrated consistently among the leaders; an ordinary N-H indole amide is already present initially.
The bridged saturated core lacks specified stereochemistry and demonstrated feasible geometry.
Independent plausible frameworks expressing the same useful functional arrangement are scarce among within-seed leaders; the observed scores identify no exact absent target pharmacophore.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxyindole anilide scores 0.3051048083696145. Child leaders reach 0.43495883620084, 0.4387992465191 and 0.4484138510190879 in seeds 0, 1 and 2; the zero-score fragment N is a clear low-context contrast. The seed-2 leader's phenyl-to-pyridyl late relative scores 0.35363976222940574, and a late charged N=N representation reaches 0.3393671624342461. Nearby halogen/side-chain variants share 0.436818201428663, so local elaboration is not uniformly rewarded. The positive association is the combined aromatic/carbonyl organization, not a requirement for reactive N substitution. Matched Child-minus-Parent endpoints are +0.04090741552648269, -0.035317771615405946 and +0.00944134898200688. Richer or more conventional-looking cores therefore do not show a uniform seed advantage. Actual source ancestry: seed 0 leader follows best real source score 0.4031937733859023, increases it by 0.03176506281493774, and is actually drawn later as a parent; seed 1 leader follows best real source score 0.4013778137849945, increases it by 0.03742143273410553, and is terminal, with no subsequent breeding opportunity; seed 2 leader follows best real source score 0.4207408531749377, increases it by 0.02767299784415017, and is actually drawn later as a parent. These sources can overlap through crossover and earlier common ancestors; local source beats and later use do not attribute a donated chemical motif or explain the matched endpoint effect.

per_task.generated_character: Medium to very large linked and fused aza-aromatic/carbonyl systems dominate, with nitrogen heterocycles, lactam-like carbonyls, ethers, nitriles, cyanates, alkene/alkyne side chains and fluorine/chlorine. The leading seed-1 structure links several dense fused regions and multiple alkoxy/nitrile substituents; nearby high-scoring relatives are much smaller. Seed 0 concentrates on linked nitrogen-rich carbonyl heterocycles with formyl substitution; seed 2 makes long repeated aza-dione/heteroaryl assemblies with fluoroalkyl esters and conjugated linkers. Mean proposal SMILES length is 84.0, maximum 217, and halogen-text incidence 0.8632. Compared with Parent's compact seed-0 nitrogen-rich carbonyl/thione leader, the Child's corresponding leader is a different lower-scoring linked carbonyl family. Large structures, cyanate bonds and dense fused topology make synthetic plausibility questionable despite recognizable subunits.
liabilities: O-linked cyanate is chemically different from an ordinary carbon-linked nitrile; other proposals contain a peroxide O-O-F ester attachment.
Multiple repeated heteroaryl/dione regions, many formyl and ester groups and conjugated linkers can greatly increase complexity without establishing improved reward.
Dense aromatic-labelled heterocycles and ring junctions require geometric checks beyond ring counts.
missing_features: The Child does not reproduce the high-scoring compact linked nitrogen/carbonyl organization seen in Parent seed 0; this is an observed coverage difference, not proof that Parent's reactive attachments are necessary.
Stable peripheral alternatives to cyanate and reactive heteroatom attachments are not systematically established at comparable score.
The leading large assemblies lack demonstrated synthesis, manageable conformations and chemically independent simplified frameworks; no exact missing pharmacophore follows from the scores.

per_task.generated_character: Medium to large aromatic amines with saturated rings dominate. Seed 1's leader combines a bridged aniline-like nitrogen core, a piperidine-like tertiary amine and a sulfoxide-linked dichloro azaaryl group. Seed 2 makes a substituted piperazine-like ring between a cyclohexene/fluoro-methoxy-aniline region and a brominated aryl thiol/benzyl-bromide region. Seed 0 has a crowded sulfur-nitrogen bridged ring and an aminoalkyl-substituted pyrrole/aryl assembly. Basic aliphatic nitrogen centres are already available: zero formal-charge-text incidence is not an absence of amines. Mean proposal SMILES length is 62.6 and halogen incidence 0.9908. Parent includes flexible tertiary aryl amines and pyrrolidine/fused-thioether families; Child leaders are generally more bridged or densely substituted. Recognizable amine rings are plausible building blocks, but their assembled geometry and reactive side groups remain questionable.
liabilities: The seed-2 leader combines benzylic bromide, aryl bromine and thiol with considerable aromatic surface.
Crowded bridged nitrogen and sulfur-imine connectivity requires geometric and stereochemical assessment; sulfoxide also has possible stereochemical identity.
The later N-F analogue introduces a reactive bond without a visible score advantage.
missing_features: Stereochemical identity is unspecified at potentially stereogenic bridged, substituted cyclic and sulfoxide environments.

Comparable useful assemblies without benzylic bromide, excessive halogen mass or difficult bridge geometry are not systematically established; conventional carbon-bound halogens need not be removed universally.
Resolved protonation/conformation is absent from this representation, but no score penalty or exact missing receptor-binding group is identified from these trajectories.

per_task.generated_character: Medium nitrogen-rich aromatic/dicarbonyl frameworks with alkoxy and short alkyl substituents dominate. Seed 0's best is a densely fused aromatic N-N/pyrrolic assembly bearing an imide/lactam-like dicarbonyl region and ethoxy substitution. Seed 1 retains a larger fused pyrrolic/aryl system with an unusual aromatic-labelled medium ring with a cyclic N-methyl urea-carbonyl region; seed 2 combines ethoxy-substituted unsaturated bridged nitrogen-dicarbonyl rings with an ethyl azaaryl region. Dense ring junctions and N-N-containing alternatives prevent treating the whole set as straightforward synthesis targets.
liabilities: Dense fused and bridged junctions may impose difficult geometry despite parseable aromatic labels.
N-N bonds and late extended nitrogen sequences are separate chemical concerns from ordinary lactam/imide nitrogen.

missing_features: Chemically independent, geometrically credible ways of expressing the favorable aromatic/dicarbonyl arrangement are not demonstrated consistently among the within-seed leaders.
Potentially stereogenic saturated and bridged centres remain unspecified.
The modest score span does not identify an exact missing pharmacophore, donor pattern or ring count; adding nitrogen or rings alone has no established benefit.

per_task.generated_character: Distinct seed families are visible. Seed 0's best is a relatively compact fluoro-phenol with a branched enamine/fluoroalkene chain, N-N-F substitution, urea-like carbonyl and terminal N-formyl group. Compared with Parent's fluorinated imino/carbonyl leaders, Child does not remove the N-halogen/geometry liabilities and has different arrangements of the same broad functional classes. Makeability is particularly questionable for the N-F and highly constrained unsaturated examples.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source ancestry: n-c55c3d520a2c, carried unchanged by same-code baseline n-62daf219c70a, now re-observed in n-dd2b25d32925. Applicability: exchange-disabled L01 graph/count-GP lineage, frozen Search seeds 0/1/2, 300 observations including ten initial, batch ten and matched Research in Depth profile. Current leaders and late relatives contain amide N-Cl, amide N-S, N-N-F and heterocyclic N-F, O-linked cyanate, benzyl bromide and an O-O-F ester attachment. Ordinary aryl halogens, an initial N-H aryl amide and high-scoring tertiary/cyclic amines also occur. The missing capability is consistent environment-specific chemistry, not absence of rings, amines or halogenation.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve conventional local bond environments while retaining useful aromatic, carbonyl and amine organization.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-agnostic transformations should distinguish local bonding environments and offer conventional alternatives while retaining functional-group relationships supported by actual feedback. A universal halogen or nitrogen ban would erase useful chemistry. Current associations do not establish that filtering raises reward or identify a covariance-mediated chemical effect.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source ancestry: n-c55c3d520a2c, carried unchanged by same-code baseline n-62daf219c70a, now re-observed in n-dd2b25d32925. Applicability: exchange-disabled L01 graph/count-GP lineage, frozen Search seeds 0/1/2, 300 observations including ten initial, batch ten and matched Research in Depth profile. Current output includes a cyclobutadiene-like ring in a fluorinated imino-carbonyl leader, dense fused N-N-containing aromatic systems and crowded bridged amines. Other high-scoring examples contain ordinary cyclic tertiary amines or open enamine chains. Rich ring-string incidence therefore coexists with both recognizable and questionable topologies; unusual fusion is not a universal requirement.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably distinguish graph-valid fused and bridged rings from geometrically credible unsaturation and connectivity.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring transformations need ring-size, bridge and bond-geometry awareness, together with alternative feasible topologies preserving learned functional arrangements. Do not treat ring count or aromatic labels as feasibility certification, or ban all small/fused rings. Neither the descriptor patterns nor their score associations isolate component contribution.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source ancestry: n-c55c3d520a2c, carried unchanged by same-code baseline n-62daf219c70a, now re-observed in n-dd2b25d32925. Applicability: exchange-disabled L01 graph/count-GP lineage, frozen Search seeds 0/1/2, 300 observations including ten initial, batch ten and matched Research in Depth profile. Stereocentre-string incidence remains 0.0 for every task, while cited bridged amines, fluorinated saturated rings and sulfoxide-bearing structures have potentially stereogenic environments. Neutral aliphatic amines also occur, so absent charge markers are a separate state-representation issue rather than evidence of missing basic centres.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not specify stereochemical identity after creating potentially stereogenic saturated, bridged and sulfur environments.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Representation and transformations should preserve or deliberately resolve stereochemistry where chemically required, distinguishing achiral and configurationally unstable cases. Protonation/tautomerism need separate treatment. The observed omission is identity uncertainty; these records do not measure a stereochemical reward penalty.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source ancestry: n-c55c3d520a2c, carried unchanged by same-code baseline n-62daf219c70a, now re-observed in n-dd2b25d32925. Applicability: exchange-disabled L01 graph/count-GP lineage, frozen Search seeds 0/1/2, 300 observations including ten initial, batch ten and matched Research in Depth profile. Accepted tiny hydrocarbons, isolated atoms and halogen fragments reach observed floors, including late emissions. At the other extreme, linked repeated heteroaryl/dione assemblies become much larger while a smaller relative retains a similar score. The full panel also contains useful compact aromatic frameworks and amines, so simplification itself is already possible and is not intrinsically harmful.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve useful molecular context while controlling fragmentation and redundant elaboration.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Use task-local observed feedback to preserve productive functional context while simplifying or replacing dispensable portions. Evidence supports testing context-aware generation rather than a fixed size threshold. Unscored surplus-pool structures have no known reward; terminal floor fragments do not show useful continuation.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source ancestry: n-c55c3d520a2c, carried unchanged by same-code baseline n-62daf219c70a, now re-observed in n-dd2b25d32925. Applicability: exchange-disabled L01 graph/count-GP lineage, frozen Search seeds 0/1/2, 300 observations including ten initial, batch ten and matched Research in Depth profile. Leading examples repeatedly alter halogen positions, short chains, N substitutions or ring segments within retained aromatic-amide, heteroaryl/dione and aryl-amine families. Different seeds do reach different frameworks, including both open chains and bridged rings; the output is not globally collapsed. Signed matched endpoint differences include both gains and losses despite rich ring coverage. Actual ancestry is overlapping and later parent draws establish use only, not donated atoms, pool-wide coverage or chemical mediation.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently supply independent plausible alternatives to a leading scaffold family within each seed.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Test scaffold reorganizations preserving observed favorable functional relationships, and assess chemical feasibility and actual productive scored descendants. Distinct SMILES, new cores and raw parent beats cannot alone establish improved discovery. Retain records with no later use and terminal censoring; absent support probabilities leave supported-but-undrawn versus zero-support classification unresolved.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
